title: Dr Reddy's Wins DCGI Approval for Zytorvi in Advanced Esophageal Cancer
excerpt: The CDSCO approval makes Zytorvi, with cisplatin and paclitaxel, a first-line option for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in India — its second indication in the country.
body:
• Dr. Reddy's Laboratories said on October 21 that the CDSCO, under the DCGI, has approved Zytorvi (toripalimab) with cisplatin and paclitaxel for first-line treatment of advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in India.
  • This is Zytorvi's second indication in India, after nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and it does not require patient selection based on PD-L1 expression.
  • In the Phase 3 JUPITER-06 trial, toripalimab plus chemotherapy cut the risk of disease progression or death by 42% versus chemotherapy alone; median overall survival was 17.7 months versus 12.9 months.
  • For patients: esophageal cancer was the fourth leading cause of cancer death in India in 2024, at about 8.1% of cancer deaths, and eligible patients can now be considered for first-line immunotherapy regardless of biomarker status.

Dr. Reddy's Laboratories said on Wednesday that the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), under the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), has approved Zytorvi (toripalimab) in combination with cisplatin and paclitaxel for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).

The approval, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine and in the company's announcement carried by EquityBulls, marks the second indication for Zytorvi in India, following its earlier approval for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

"This second indication marks an important step in extending the reach of immunotherapy to patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma."

— M.V. Ramana, Chief Executive Officer, Global Generics, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories

What was approved

Zytorvi is a monoclonal antibody that targets programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1). The Indian approval covers its use alongside cisplatin and paclitaxel as a first treatment for adults whose ESCC cannot be removed surgically, has returned, or has spread. The approved indication does not require patient selection based on PD-L1 expression, enabling appropriate patients to be considered for treatment regardless of their biomarker status — the same basis on which the European Medicines Agency approved toripalimab for first-line ESCC.

The trial behind the decision

The approval is supported by the Phase 3 JUPITER-06 trial. In the study, toripalimab in combination with paclitaxel and cisplatin reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 42% compared with chemotherapy alone. At the final overall-survival analysis, median overall survival was 17.7 months with toripalimab plus chemotherapy, compared with 12.9 months with chemotherapy alone. Clinical benefit was observed across PD-L1-expression subgroups.

Why it matters in India

In 2024, esophageal cancer was the fourth leading cause of cancer-related death in India, accounting for approximately 8.1% of all cancer deaths. ESCC, the predominant subtype, accounts for approximately 80% of all esophageal cancer cases in India. Dr. Reddy's said it aims through Zytorvi to expand access to first-line immunotherapy for appropriate patients with advanced ESCC in India.

Dr. Reddy's entered into a licensing and commercialisation agreement with Shanghai Junshi Biosciences in 2023, granting it exclusive rights to develop and market toripalimab in 21 countries, including India. Globally, toripalimab is approved by regulators including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the European Medicines Agency and the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency.

What happens next

The company did not disclose pricing or an expected revenue contribution for the expanded indication in the reports. For oncologists, the immediate change is practical: an additional first-line option for eligible advanced ESCC patients, without a PD-L1 test gate. M.V. Ramana, chief executive officer for Global Generics at Dr. Reddy's, said the company's focus remains on building its oncology portfolio and expanding access to innovative treatment options.
